1.why: All eight screens are static forms with plain cards, a header, and a text-only Logs panel; no moving images, animations, or pop-ups appear anywhere.

2.why: Bold headings, solid-blue primary buttons, and tinted notice boxes (green confirmation, 'Stay safe' panel) make key items stand out, although the dark Logs panel visually competes with the form card.

3.why: Each page presents a single clearly labeled task so the next field or button is quick to find, though Helena must look below the form into the Logs panel to locate the token and verification code.

4.why: The wizard guides step-by-step and displays the password policy, but Helena must still track a six-stage process and apply a five-rule password policy (length, upper, lower, number, symbol) from working memory.

5.why: No 'remember me', password-manager, or autofill option appears on any screen; the only fill assistance is the 'Use simulated recovery link' button that inserts the reset token.

6.why: Previously entered items remain visible and recognizable: the typed email persists on step 2, the reset token is pre-filled on step 3, and the consent checkbox appears pre-ticked on step 7.

7.why: Sentences are short and plain (e.g., 'Paste the token from your simulated recovery message'), but technical terms such as 'reset token', 'MFA', and 'simulated link' remain.

8.why: No error message appears in any of the eight screenshots, only success confirmations, so nothing demonstrates that errors describe the problem and how to fix it.

9.why: No illustrative examples (sample email or sample password) are provided, although the Logs panel and pre-filled field do show the exact token and code to type.

10.why: The choices that exist ('Request reset instructions' vs 'Enter a reset token', 'Verify' vs 'Back') are clearly labeled, visually distinct buttons, even though no alternative methods like face login are offered.

11.why: No screen ever presents more than three buttons, so the user is never faced with too many choices at one time.

12.why: Outcomes are announced via the green 'reset instructions have been prepared' banner, the final 'Conditions accepted' page, and timestamped Logs entries, though some steps signal success only by advancing to the next screen.

13.why: Each new step includes short help text or tips, such as the password rules line, the note that the code was delivered to the Logs panel, and the 'Stay safe' anti-phishing advice.

14.why: A 'Back' button and the ability to re-request reset instructions exist, but no failed-attempt screen is shown, so easy retry after a mistake is not demonstrated.

15.why: Every step reuses the same header, centered card layout, button styles, and Logs panel, so the design stays consistent and learnable across the whole flow.
